items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: But I mean Bach would have been a fantastic jazz musician.

ctx.x: That’s great. I saw a thing that you said which really caught my eye. And it went something like, “Assume there’s nobody else, tell students to play as if there’s no one else in the rhythm section.” And the first time I went like “wow.” Some people would say, like what do you mean, the rhythm section has to be one, everybody has to be together. But then you went on to explain it. I wish you would explain it again, because I found it really very interesting.

Well bass players, I think we have, I assume you’re the only harmonic and rhythmic substance that there is. In other words, don’t — if the piano player’s not there, does that mean you can’t play? If the drummer’s not there, does that mean you can’t play with good time? So you don’t really need them. And they don’t need you either. If they play with good time and good sense of harmony and everything, that’s how solo pianists can — I mean the piano is an orchestra, so I mean they can do a lot more things obviously,…
You sort of played it first by trial and error, then learned why it sounded good?
